author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. Shakespeare made government a matter of public performance and private knowledge. This play tests a ruler's claim to enforce virtue by giving him power over someone whose vulnerability becomes a temptation.

hook.text: Would you trust a judge who has never had to face his own temptation?

paragraphs: A deputy is left to enforce laws that have long been neglected. His severity quickly puts a young man's life at risk. The man's sister comes to ask for mercy and discovers that moral authority may conceal a private appetite.

The play brings law, desire and power into a deeply unequal conversation. A person can demand purity from others while finding reasons why his own conduct deserves an exception. Those subject to authority have fewer ways to make their account believed.

Shakespeare also questions the comforts of a ruler who watches from a distance and arranges events behind the scenes. Solving a problem can become another way of possessing the people inside it. The comic elements do not make the pressures less serious.
Read for who gets a choice and who is handed an apparent solution. How much would you trust a just outcome if someone else had decided what you must accept?

orientation.text: The Duke temporarily hands authority to Angelo. Isabella's appeal introduces the central conflict; the Duke's concealed presence gives the audience knowledge other characters lack.
